correctness.rationale: The quotient is well defined modulo p^k on input classes modulo p^(k+1). Each admissible residue class r in 1,...,p-2 is a graph of p^k points: the Teichmuller-based quotient map has unit derivative with a one-power valuation drop. For distinct r,s, equality of both quotient coordinates gives a 2x2 Teichmuller linear system with unit determinant mod p (r-s), so exactly one pairwise intersection. A triple exact common point yields three distinct complex numbers on circles centered at 0 and 1, impossible. Nonzero cyclotomic numerator has every conjugate bounded by 8, hence rational norm <=8^phi(p-1); any triple mod p^k forces this integer norm divisible by p^(k+1), contradicting k cutoff. Multiplication by h maps the two coordinates by a unit affine map and preserves multiplicities. The p=3 one-branch and p=11,k=1 triple-fiber boundaries are explicit. Independently enumerated full periods p=3,k1,2; p=5,k3; p=7,k3; p=11,k1,2 and unit shifts (5,2,2),(7,2,3). This is not an infinite computational proof.

value.rationale: The exact image and fiber distribution of two neighboring Fermat quotients across all prime powers is a natural arithmetic distribution invariant. Exact pairwise intersection and effective stabilization constitute substantive structure, not merely finite tabulation, and distinguish a strict high-exponent law from the demonstrated low-exponent triple overlap.

final_claim: For each odd prime p, each h coprime to p, and k with p^k >= 8^phi(p-1), neighboring Fermat-quotient pairs modulo p^k have only single and double fibers; exactly C(p-2,2) double targets and image size (p-2)p^k-C(p-2,2).
